goal: Create a dense but readable city food-walk map that combines tourism landmarks, local food spots, route guidance, and collectible poster charm.
style: watercolor and ink hand-drawn illustration on vintage parchment, editorial travel-poster finish, charming but practical wayfinding design

title_section.text: 成都 吃货暴走地图
title_section.subtitle: 一张能看、能逛、能吃的城市美食导览图
title_section.mascot: cartoon red chili pepper wearing sunglasses and giving a thumbs up

border: decorative vine border of green leaves and red chili peppers, thin hand-drawn frame, playful but not cluttered

layout.background: textured beige parchment paper with yellow roads, blue rivers, pale green park areas, subtle street blocks, clean map hierarchy
layout.centerpiece: giant panda sitting and eating bamboo, integrated naturally near the city center as the visual anchor

sections.title: landmarks
illustrations: traditional pavilion in a city park
modern skyscraper with a climbing panda sculpture motif
traditional gate and old alley entrance

sections.title: food_spots
sections.purpose: numbered food discoveries distributed around the map like a walking quest

bottom_right_extras: vintage compass rose with N, S, E, W
small disclaimer text: 温馨提示：吃辣需谨慎，肠胃要保护~ with a red chili pepper icon

text_rules: Use large, legible Chinese labels only.
Prefer short labels over paragraph text.
Avoid tiny microtext and fake sponsor logos.
Keep numbering 1 to 12 visually clear and consistent.
negative_prompt: photorealistic satellite map, generic flat vector UI, tiny unreadable text, dense paragraph blocks, fake logos, sponsor banners, visual clutter, random cars, unrelated people, extra landmarks not requested, dark moody lighting, heavy shadows, glossy highlights, perspective distortion, messy route lines, broken Chinese characters, duplicated icons, overdecorated border
quality_notes: Treat the image as a polished wayfinding poster, not a fantasy illustration only.
The map must remain readable at a glance.
